cases.description: Message contains an A record for example.com. in the ANSWER section. The first call to findRRset(name, type, Section.ANSWER) returns true, so the overall method returns true without checking other sections.
No MX record for example.org. in ANSWER, but one exists in the AUTHORITY section. The first call returns false, the second call (AUTHORITY) returns true, causing the overall result to be true.
The TXT record for example.net. is absent from ANSWER and AUTHORITY sections but present in the ADDITIONAL section. The method returns true after the third call succeeds.
The queried name/type combination does not exist in any of the three sections. All three internal findRRset calls return false, so the method returns false.
Passing a null Name should cause a NullPointerException (or the method’s internal validation to throw). The test verifies that the exception is thrown.
An invalid DNS type (negative value) is supplied. The internal findRRset implementation treats it as not matching any record, so all three section checks return false and the method returns false.

Message contains an A record for example.com. in both ANSWER and AUTHORITY sections. The first internal call (ANSWER) returns true, so the overall method returns true without invoking the AUTHORITY or ADDITIONAL checks.
No NS record in ANSWER, but one exists in AUTHORITY. The method returns false after the first check, true after the second, and never evaluates ADDITIONAL.
Message has no records in any section. All three internal findRRset calls return false, so the method returns false.

group: findRRset ANY type matches any record

cases.description: Message contains an MX record for example.com. in the ANSWER section. Using the ANY type (255) should match any existing RRset for the name, causing the method to return true.
Message stores an A record with the canonical name "example.com." in the ANSWER section. DNS names are case‑insensitive, so a mixed‑case query should still locate the RRset and return true.
A type value larger than the maximum 16‑bit DNS type is supplied. The internal findRRset implementation treats it as non‑matching, resulting in false for all sections.
Message contains an A record for the parent name "example.com." but the query asks for the subdomain "sub.example.com.". No exact match exists in any section, so the method returns false.
Name does not end with a trailing dot, therefore it is not an absolute DNS name. The method validates the name and throws IllegalArgumentException.
Name contains illegal characters. The DNS library rejects it during validation and the method throws IllegalArgumentException.
Empty string is not a valid DNS name; the method throws IllegalArgumentException.
Type value exceeds the 16‑bit DNS type limit (0‑65535). The implementation checks the range and throws IllegalArgumentException.
Negative type values are invalid. The method validates the argument and throws IllegalArgumentException.

group: findRRset type not allowed in section

cases.description: SIG0 records are not permitted in the ANSWER, AUTHORITY, or ADDITIONAL sections for a standard query. The internal check `isTypeAllowedInSection` throws IllegalArgumentException when the type is disallowed.
